1. (Currently amended) A control system comprising: a controller including a processor and memory, wherein the controller is communicatively coupled to automation components in the control system and configured to facilitate performance of a process through interoperation with the automation components by generating holistic state data, wherein the controller generates the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, a model configured to describe the process used by the controller; determining, using the processor, input and output variables of the process; determining, using the processor, constraints on the input and output variables; determining, using the processor, an objective function associated with the process used by the controller; and storing, in the memory, the model, the input and output variables, the constraints, and the objective function in one of a plurality of fields in the holistic state data to enable the automation components to detect and operate with the controller upon receiving the holistic state data, wherein the holistic state data is transmitted to the automation components to control physical operations of the automation components in the process.

2. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is communicatively coupled to the automation components via a communication network and communicates the holistic state data to each of the automation components upon connecting to the communication network to control the physical operations of the automation components.

3. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is communicatively coupled to the automation components via a backplane and communicates the holistic state data to the automation components upon connecting to the backplane to control the physical operations of the automation components.

4. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the holistic state data is in a standardized format understood by each of the automation components, and wherein the standardized format enables interoperability among the automation components.

5. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller generates the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, an intermediate search result of an optimization search; determining, using the processor, a state of the optimization search when the intermediate search result is determined; and storing, in the memory, the intermediate search result and the state in an optimization state field of the holistic state data.

6. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller generates the holistic state data to facilitate performing an optimization search in conjunction with one or more of the automation components in the control system, wherein the optimization search determines control actions for the automation components.

7. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller generates the holistic state data by: determining, using the processor, computational capabilities of the controller; determining, using the processor, interconnections with the automation components in the control system; and storing, in the memory, the computational capabilities and the interconnections in a controller settings field of the holistic state data.

8. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller communicates the holistic state data to a server in the control system to facilitate determining an optimization problem for controlling the automation components.

9. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller comprises the memory configured as an in-memory database to store the holistic state data.

10. (Currently amended) A tangible, non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to store instructions executable by a processor of a controller, wherein the instructions comprise instructions to: receive, using the processor, control system configuration data comprising holistic state data from automation components; determine, using the processor, the automation components communicatively coupled to the controller and characteristics of the automation components based at least in part on parsing the control system configuration data; determine, using the processor, an optimization problem based at least in part on the automation components and the characteristics of each of the automation components, wherein the optimization problem specifies control objectives and constraints for the automation components; and instruct, using the processor, one or more of the automation components to perform a control action in a process, wherein the control action is determined based at least in part on solving the optimization problem.

11. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a model used by the automation component to control its operations, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on the model used by each of the automation components.

12. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a computing capability of the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on computing capabilities and compatibilities of each of the automation components.

13. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the control system configuration data comprises a plurality of holistic state data, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data corresponds with one of the automation components and is received from that automation component.

14. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein the instructions to determine the automation components and characteristics of the automation components comprise instructions to parse each of the plurality of holistic state data received from the automation components.

15. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data comprises a standardized format with same fields, enabling interoperability among the automation components.

16. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the instructions to receive the configuration data comprise instructions to receive the configuration data from a cloud computing system.

17. (Currently amended) A method for performing diagnostics on a control system comprising: determining, using a processor, holistic state data captured by a controller in the control system, wherein the holistic state data includes a model, input and output variables, constraints, and an objective function for a process; simulating, using the processor, operation of the controller based at least in part on the holistic state data while the controller performs other operations, wherein the simulating includes executing the model with various control actions; analyzing, using the processor, the simulation of the controller to perform diagnostics on the controller and the process; and adjusting, using the processor, operation of the control system based at least in part on the diagnostics to improve performance of the process.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein: simulating operation comprises simulating performance of various control actions by the controller on the process; and analyzing the simulation comprises analyzing results of the various control actions on the process.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein analyzing the simulation comprises: determining, using the processor, a predicted response to a control action determined by the controller using the model; and comparing, using the processor, the predicted response with an actual response to the control action to determine accuracy of the model.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, comprising adjusting, using the processor, the model when the predicted response and the actual response vary by more than a threshold amount.
